title: News Releases | National Institutes of Health (NIH)
content: News Releases Media Inquiries NIH on Social Media Images and B-roll Calendar of Events NIH News Publications News Releases Search NIH news releases Search Filter by Year (optional) - Any - 2025 2024 2023 2022 2021 2020 2019 2018 NIH researchers identify avenue for enhanced GLP-1-induced weight loss May 22, 2026 — Modulating intracellular signaling may extend drug effects. NIH-supported project expands access to care for children with amblyopia May 15, 2026 — Open-access tool guides eye doctors without specific pediatric eye care training in amblyopia diagnosis and management. Researchers identify first suite of human antibodies against measles virus May 14, 2026 — NIH-funded study lays foundation for antibody-based measles treatment. NIH-funded study maps human pancreatic islet cells, offering new clues to diabetes risk May 12, 2026 — Comprehensive characterization of islet cells facilitated by national organ donation program. Researchers develop innovative model for risk assessment for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy May 11, 2026 — NIH-funded study incorporates new measures to better predict outcomes in chronic heart condition. NIH-funded study suggests that testosterone suppresses brain tumor growth in males May 6, 2026 — Findings may warrant exploration of the hormones as glioblastoma treatment. Oral small-molecule GLP-1 drugs penetrate deep into the brain to suppress cravings May 6, 2026 — NIH-funded research identifies new mechanism of action for next-generation weight-loss drugs. Adding weekly GLP-1 to cognitive behavioral therapy further reduces heavy drinking April 30, 2026 — Clinical trial suggests semaglutide may help patients with alcohol use disorder and obesity. Symptom-based approach treats opioid withdrawal in newborns with minimal drug exposure April 27, 2026 — NIH-funded clinical trial shows that the new approach could also decrease time in the hospital. Clinical trial finds no difference in fluid treatment options for pediatric sepsis April 24, 2026 — NIH-supported study is largest ever to compare fluid interventions to prevent major kidney damage in children treated for septic shock.
